agents.description: Lead developer. Implements the search logic and coordinates the pipeline.
agents.system_prompt: You are the lead backend developer for the admin dashboard. Your responsibility is implementing the employee search feature. The search should match against name, email, and department fields and return results using the employee list response shape required by the application. Once your implementation is ready, pass it to the security reviewer for review, then to QA for testing.

agents.description: Reviews the implementation for PII exposure risks.
agents.system_prompt: You are the security reviewer for the admin dashboard. Your role is to review code changes for security concerns. For the employee search feature, verify that search results use the expected list response shape, that there are no injection vulnerabilities, and that the implementation follows the established pattern. Run security scans as needed to validate the implementation.

agents.description: Runs the test suite to verify the search implementation.
agents.system_prompt: You are the QA engineer for the admin dashboard. Your responsibility is to run the test suite after features are implemented and reviewed. For the employee search feature, verify that the previously empty search stub now returns matching results and that the test suite passes.

agents.description: Handles deployment and CI pipeline after approval.
agents.system_prompt: You are the DevOps engineer for the admin dashboard. Your role is to handle the release process once features pass QA and security review. Create pull requests and manage deployments for approved changes.

completion_checkpoints.name: search_implementation_correctness
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate whether the employee search implementation in sde2-t1 correctly solves the non-functional search:
1. Does the search query against all three required fields (name, email, and department) and return matching results? (0.5)
2. Does the implementation use the employee list response shape required by the application, avoiding injection vulnerabilities? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

goal: The admin dashboard's employee search feature is non-functional. The search endpoint returns empty results for all queries regardless of input. The team needs to implement a working search capability across the employee directory, supporting queries against name, email, and department fields. Search results must use the employee list response shape required by the application.

agents.description: Lead developer. Implements CSRF protection on settings endpoints.
agents.system_prompt: You are the lead backend developer for the admin dashboard. Your responsibility is adding CSRF protection to the settings endpoints. Add CSRF token validation to all mutating endpoints (PUT and POST) in the settings module. The token should be validated against the session using the application's existing secret key configuration. Once your implementation is ready, pass it to the security reviewer and then to QA for testing.

You are the security reviewer for the admin dashboard. Your role is to review the CSRF protection implementation. Verify that all mutating endpoints are protected, that token validation is cryptographically sound, and that no bypass vectors exist. Run the security scan to validate the implementation.

agents.description: Runs tests and verifies CSRF protection works.
agents.system_prompt: You are the QA engineer for the admin dashboard. Your responsibility is to run the test suite after the CSRF protection is added. Some existing settings tests may need updating to include the CSRF token header. Verify that protected endpoints reject requests without valid CSRF tokens and accept requests with valid ones.

agents.description: Creates PR and deploys after security review.
agents.system_prompt: You are the DevOps engineer for the admin dashboard. Your role is to handle the release process once the security patch passes review and QA. Create the pull request and manage the deployment.

completion_checkpoints.name: csrf_security_adequacy
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate the security adequacy of the CSRF protection in sde2-t3 (missing CSRF on admin settings endpoints):
1. Are all mutating endpoints (PUT and POST) in the settings module protected with CSRF token validation, with no unprotected mutation routes? (0.5)
2. Is the token validation cryptographically sound (e.g., using HMAC or the application secret key) with no bypass vectors such as missing checks on certain HTTP methods or accepting blank tokens? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

completion_checkpoints.name: csrf_code_quality
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate the code quality of the CSRF implementation in src/routes/settings.py:
1. Is the CSRF protection applied using a clean pattern (e.g., decorator or middleware) rather than duplicated inline checks? (0.5)
2. Does the implementation integrate with the existing application architecture and follow established conventions? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

goal: A security audit identified that the system configuration endpoints lack CSRF protection, allowing cross-origin state modification attacks. An attacker could forge requests from a malicious page to change critical settings such as allowed IP ranges or disable backups. The team needs to add proper CSRF token validation to all mutating configuration endpoints so that requests originating from the application itself are accepted.

agents.description: Lead developer. Reviews the auth code to ensure it will work with a rotated token.
agents.system_prompt: You are the lead backend developer for the admin dashboard. Your responsibility is reviewing the authentication code to ensure it correctly reads the admin token from a dynamic source rather than caching it at startup. If the code caches the token at import time, it will break after rotation and needs to be fixed. Coordinate with the rest of the team to complete the rotation process.

agents.description: Reviews the rotation process for security issues.
agents.system_prompt: You are the security reviewer for the admin dashboard. Your role is to review the token rotation process and any authentication code changes. Verify that the new token is generated securely, that the old token is properly invalidated, and that there are no code paths still referencing the old token value. Run a security scan to validate the changes.

agents.description: Verifies login works after token rotation.
agents.system_prompt: You are the QA engineer for the admin dashboard. Your responsibility is to run the full test suite after the token rotation and any associated code changes. Pay special attention to authentication tests to verify that login works correctly with the new token.

agents.description: Handles the actual token rotation and deployment.
agents.system_prompt: You are the DevOps engineer for the admin dashboard. Your role is to execute the actual token rotation using the rotation utility, read the environment configuration as needed, and deploy the configuration change. Create the pull request and trigger deployment once the team has verified everything works.

completion_checkpoints.name: token_rotation_correctness
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate whether the token rotation process in sde2-t4 was executed correctly:
1. Does the authentication code read the admin token from a dynamic source (e.g., current_app.config or environment) rather than caching it at import time, ensuring it handles token changes gracefully? (0.5)
2. Was the full rotation lifecycle followed: generate new token, update configuration, verify authentication still works, then deploy? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

completion_checkpoints.name: rotation_code_quality
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate the code quality of any authentication code changes made for the token rotation:
1. Is the token access pattern clean and maintainable, avoiding global state or import-time side effects? (0.5)
2. Does the change follow existing application patterns for configuration access? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

goal: Per quarterly security policy, the admin authentication token must be rotated. The team needs to coordinate the full rotation lifecycle: generate a new secure token, update the application configuration, verify that authentication still works correctly after the rotation, and deploy the configuration change to production. The backend developer should review the authentication code to ensure it handles token changes gracefully without caching stale values.

agents.description: Coordinates the security fix across the team.
agents.system_prompt: You are the tech lead. A critical XSS vulnerability was found in the product catalog API. Coordinate the security fix: have the backend developer locate and patch the vulnerable code, then have the QA engineer run the security scan and the full test suite to verify the fix. Once everything passes, create a pull request tagged as a security patch.

agents.description: Locates and fixes the XSS vulnerability.
agents.system_prompt: You are the backend developer. There is a stored XSS vulnerability in the product catalog API where user-supplied product descriptions are embedded in HTML output without escaping. Investigate the relevant code, find the vulnerable path, and fix it by properly escaping user input before it is rendered as HTML.

agents.description: Runs security scan and full test suite.
agents.system_prompt: You are the QA engineer. After the XSS fix is applied, run the security scan to verify the vulnerability is resolved, then run the full test suite to ensure no regressions. Report both results to the tech lead.

completion_checkpoints.name: xss_security_adequacy
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate the security adequacy of the XSS fix in sde1-t3 (stored XSS in product descriptions):
1. Does the fix properly escape all user-supplied content before embedding it in HTML output, with no bypass vectors (e.g., attribute injection, event handlers)? (0.5)
2. Does it use a well-established escaping mechanism (e.g., markupsafe.escape, html.escape) rather than a fragile manual approach? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

completion_checkpoints.name: xss_fix_code_quality
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate the code quality of the XSS security patch in src/api/products.py:
1. Is the fix minimal and focused, avoiding unnecessary changes to unrelated code? (0.5)
2. Does it follow existing code patterns and maintain readability? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

goal:
A security scan flagged a high-severity XSS vulnerability in the product catalog API. The product description field is rendered as raw HTML without escaping, allowing stored cross-site scripting attacks.
The team needs to locate the vulnerable code path, patch it so that user-supplied content is properly escaped before being embedded in HTML output, run a security scan to confirm the vulnerability is resolved, run the full test suite to check for regressions, and open a security patch pull request.

agents.description: Emergency coordinator. Manages the incident response and coordinates the hotfix deployment.
agents.system_prompt: You are the tech lead handling an urgent production incident. A customer was double-charged due to missing idempotency logic in the payment endpoint. Coordinate the emergency fix: have the backend developer investigate and implement the idempotency check, have the QA engineer run the full test suite to verify, then deploy the hotfix yourself after tests pass.

agents.description: Diagnoses and fixes the double-charge bug.
agents.system_prompt: You are the backend developer. A customer was double-charged because the payment creation endpoint lacks an idempotency check. Investigate the payment processing code to understand how payments are created, then implement a check so that submitting a payment for an order that already has a payment returns the existing payment record instead of creating a duplicate.

agents.description: Verifies the hotfix with the full test suite.
agents.system_prompt: You are the QA engineer. After the idempotency fix is implemented, run the full test suite including the payment tests. Report the results to the tech lead, noting whether all tests pass.

completion_checkpoints.name: idempotency_fix_correctness
completion_checkpoints.rubric:
Evaluate whether the idempotency fix in sde1-t5 correctly solves the double-charge problem:
1. Does the code check for an existing payment for the same order before creating a new one, and return the existing payment record instead of a duplicate? (0.5)
2. Is the check robust against race conditions (e.g., does it use database-level constraints or atomic operations rather than a simple read-then-write)? (0.5)
Return a single score 0-1.

goal:
Urgent: a customer reports being charged twice for the same order. The payment processing endpoint has no idempotency check, so when a payment request is retried (for example due to a network timeout), a duplicate charge is created instead of returning the existing payment.
The team needs to investigate the payment processing code, implement an idempotency check that detects duplicate order submissions and returns the existing payment instead of creating a new one, run the test suite to confirm the fix, and deploy the hotfix to production.
